line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 d4 Bb4
teaches: Before making a capture in the centre, check whether the piece you are counting on to recapture is pinned. A bishop pinning a knight against the king does not have to win material to matter — it removes that knight from every calculation, and captures that looked safe stop being safe.
explains: The bishop on b4 pins the knight on c3 against the king, and that knight has no legal move at all. So taking on e5 loses a pawn outright: Black takes on e4 and there is no recapture, because the only piece that guards it cannot move. Pushing the d-pawn past instead gains space and forces the knight on c6 to find a new square.
